messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran a multi-hour perf sweep on the 8k route. p95 is OK but p99 tail is spiking when KV hits eviction under mixed prompt lengths.

samir: Could you paste the top-line numbers?

maria: baseline p95 ~210ms, p99 ~1.3s, tail 99.9 ~2.8s for a sustained batch load. When kv-evict-rate > 40% we see a jump.

devon: Is kernel selection changing under those evictions? i.e., are we falling back to slower kernels because sequence lengths shift?

maria: Yes — profiler shows kernel-switch churn when requests require fresh KV rebuilds. Kernel overhead + cache miss = ~300-500ms extra per affected microbatch.

hannah: Any correlation with microbatch size? We recently pushed microbatch=16 default on that pool.

maria: Good call — with microbatch=8 the p99 drops to ~900ms, but throughput drops ~18%. Microbatch=32 increases p95 slightly but p99 becomes awful.

samir: So classic latency SLO vs throughput tradeoff. Do we have a recommended policy for routes that care about p99?

maria: Proposal: adaptive microbatch caps per route + soft max_tokens cap when KV eviction rate climbs. Example heuristic: if kv_eviction_rate > 30% and p99 > 1s -> reduce microbatch target by 50% and cap max_tokens to 2048 for new requests.

bench-bot: perf snapshot uploaded: https://internal/bench/1780012345/snap1 flamegraph + timeline.

ops-bot: Alert rule RL-RT-8k fired 3x in last 2h for tail-latency > 1.5s.

devon: Can we avoid global caps? Maybe per-tenant adaptive truncation: if the request hits eviction, return a structured warning + truncated flag and short-circuit further token generation.

maria: I sketched a lightweight protocol: client receives "x-truncated":true header and a small token-count hint. That lets higher-level apps decide to re-issue with longer budget when needed.

hannah: OTOH clients expect monotonic behavior. We should ensure deterministic truncation: e.g., prefer suffix-drop for multi-turn chat vs prefix-drop for single-turn long completion.

samir: Also need the runtime to prefer cheaper kernels when eviction spike detected — avoid kernel switch thrash. Maybe pin kernel selection for N minutes for a given model on that node.

maria: Pinning could reduce churn but may increase average latency if pinned kernel isn't optimal for some sequence lengths. We need a hysteresis window: pin for 60s then re-evaluate.

devon: Implementation sketch (config snippet):
```
route: /v1/generate
  adaptive_policy:
    kv_eviction_threshold: 0.30
    microbatch_shrink_factor: 0.5
    max_tokens_soft_cap: 2048
    kernel_pin_ttl_seconds: 60
    truncation_mode: route_defined # client-signal for chat vs completion
```

maria: Also added a metric: kernel_switch_count_per_minute and avg_kv_rebuild_time. We should drive autoscaler to spin up nodes when kv_rebuild_time > 200ms.

hannah: What about timeouts? I've seen requests hang waiting for rebuild; a hard per-token timeout (like 800ms) might be needed to protect tails.

samir: Hard timeouts are blunt. Prefer staged timeouts: token_generation_timeout (soft) -> emit partial -> final_timeout (hard) -> abort with code. That matches graceful degradation.

maria: Agree. Proposed defaults for 8k route: token_generation_soft=750ms, final_timeout=2s. Soft timeout triggers early truncation + client header.

devon: We should add an e2e test in perf harness: synthetic mix with KV churn, varying microbatch sizes, validate p95/p99 and correct headers.

hannah: I'll add test cases. Maria, can you trim the flamegraph to the hot paths and assign follow-ups to infra?

maria: Yup — uploading trimmed traces and opening a PR for the adaptive_policy.

ops-bot: Created ticket RT-4821: "adaptive microbatch & truncation for KV eviction tail mitigation" assigned to eng-runtime.

samir: Thanks team. Let's iterate on conservative defaults first, monitor client impact, then tune for throughput. :thumbsup:
